hints.S08_A1: The mall is compared to a BEEHIVE, with SHOPPERS MOVING IN EVERY DIRECTION. Ask: is a beehive quiet, empty and dark, or humming with constant activity? Match the adjective to the movement, not to the building.
hints.S08_A2: The clue is BY HALF, during the YEAR-END SALE. Ask: in a sale, does a price climb or come down? 'Raised' and 'doubled' both push it up, and 'ignored' does nothing to it at all.
hints.S08_A3: Ben COMPARED PRICES at three stores first, so he spent the forty dollars on purpose, as a treat. Ask: do 'throw away' or 'give away' fit money he meant to spend? 'Run out of' means having none left.
hints.S08_A4: The owner's RELIEF AND GRATITUDE MADE HIS DAY. Ask: does the idiom describe someone bursting with happiness, or someone ill, in trouble, or confused? An idiom cannot be worked out word by word.
hints.S08_A5: The WET MARKET is packed with SHOPPERS hunting for FRESH INGREDIENTS before a FEAST. Ask: could 'silent', 'deserted' or 'empty' ever fit a market full of people? The blank needs the opposite of empty.
hints.S08_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not THE FAMILY. Words like nobody and everyone behave like ONE person. Ask: does a singular subject take the plain present verb, or the one ending in -s? The -ing form is not used with this thinking verb.
hints.S08_B2: HAS is already in the sentence, so the blank must be its partner. Ask: after has, do we need the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? This verb is regular, so the ending follows the usual rule.
hints.S08_B3: The customer's phone SUDDENLY RANG - that cut across something already happening. Ask: which form shows an action in progress in the past? A plain past verb would show only a finished, closed action.
hints.S08_B4: THAN sets ONLINE PRICES against IN-STORE PRICES, and the adjective is short. Ask: does a short adjective add -er, or take 'most' in front? And can you ever put 'more' before a word that already ends in -er?
hints.S08_B5: The second half gives the REASON for her choice: it was her FAVOURITE COLOUR. Ask: which joining word introduces a reason? 'So' would put a result there instead, and 'although' would signal a contrast.
hints.S08_B6: A tag mirrors the main verb, and this statement uses IS ('Spending more than you earn IS a sure way'). Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag stay positive or flip to negative? Keep the same verb - do not borrow 'do'.
hints.S08_B7: Look at the last word of the sentence: WAS. The whole scene sits in the past. Ask: is this verb regular? 'Telled' does not exist - think of sell becoming sold. Every verb in the sentence must share one time.
hints.S08_B8: Mother PAID for the shopping - a past verb - so the blank must sit in the same past time. Ask: is 'amusement' a naming word and 'amusing' a describing word? The blank needs an action that matches PAID.
hints.S08_C1: The blank stands in front of the noun MOTHER, so it must show whom she belongs to. Ask: can a subject pronoun like 'I' ever sit before a naming word? A possessive form is needed there.
hints.S08_C2: The blank comes straight after the verb TOOK, so the writer is being taken, not doing the taking. Ask: does a subject form like 'I' ever follow a verb? Test the gap on its own: 'Mother took ___'.
hints.S08_C3: This blank opens the sentence and is the subject of WANTED - the writer plus the SISTER, two people. Ask: can an object form like 'us' ever act as a subject? Say it aloud: 'Us wanted shoes' is wrong.
hints.S08_C4: Use the removal test: take away MY SISTER AND, and read what is left - '___ TRIED ON MANY PAIRS'. Ask: does a subject form or an object form fit there? The subject of TRIED can never be 'me'.
hints.S08_C5: The blank follows the verb HELPED, so the two shoppers are receiving the help, not giving it. Ask: which form comes after a verb - the subject one, or the object one? 'The assistant helped we' sounds wrong for a reason.
hints.S08_C6: The blank stands in front of the noun BELONGINGS, so it must show who owns them. Ask: can 'we' sit before a naming word? Before a noun you need a possessive form, never a subject or an object form.
hints.S08_C7: The blank follows TAKE GOOD CARE OF, so the belongings are receiving the action. Ask: after a verb and the little word 'of', do we use the subject form 'they', or its object partner? Pronouns change shape with their job.
hints.S08_C8: This blank is the subject of WILL LAST - the belongings are doing the lasting. Ask: can the object form 'them' ever act as a subject? Say it aloud: 'Them will last a long time' is wrong.
hints.S08_D1: The word STRICT and the exact sum of FIFTY DOLLARS point to a limit fixed before shopping began. Ask: which box word names the amount you decide to spend and must not go over? A receipt is only proof of what you paid.
hints.S08_D2: Compare the two figures: the ORIGINAL PRICE WAS EIGHTY DOLLARS, but she paid only FORTY-FIVE. Ask: which box word names something bought far below its normal price? The blank follows 'a great', so it is a naming word.
hints.S08_D3: You JOIN it, it is LONG, and it forms at the CUSTOMER SERVICE COUNTER. Ask: which box word names a line of people waiting for their turn? A cashier is a person, and a trolley is a thing you push.
hints.S08_D4: The blank follows ASKED TO, so it must be a doing word, and the pattern is '___ IT FOR A NEW ONE'. Ask: which box word means handing back a faulty item and taking a working one in its place?
hints.S08_D5: She has already been promised the new bag, so this last thing is given FOR THE INCONVENIENCE. Ask: which box word names money handed back to a customer? A receipt is only a slip of paper - it is not money.
hints.S08_E1: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about the CHEERFUL MUSIC reaching your ears. Ask: which of the two look-alikes has EAR hidden inside it? Choose by meaning, since both sound the same.
hints.S08_E2: Everything around it happened LAST SATURDAY, so the story is finished and past. Ask: is GO a past form, or the plain base verb? This verb is irregular - its past looks nothing like it, and 'goed' is not a word.
hints.S08_E3: TRIES carries the -s of the present tense, yet the whole passage is set in the past. Ask: what is this verb's past form? When a verb ends in -y after a consonant, the y must change before the ending is added.
hints.S08_E4: Find the subject of the underlined verb: SOME ITEMS - many things, not one. Ask: can a plural subject ever take 'was'? Match the verb to the main noun, never to the BOX that comes after it.
hints.S08_E5: The PURCHASES belong to the SHOPPERS - many owners, not one. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? When the owners are many, where must the apostrophe sit?
hints.S08_F1: The SHOPKEEPER ASKED a yes/no QUESTION and you must now report it. Ask: which small joining word follows asked? Does the reported part keep question order, or normal statement order? And what must 'you' and 'are' become?
hints.S08_F2: WHILE goes in front of the longer action that was already under way. Ask: which of the two sentences is the background action, and which one happens inside it? Keep the helping verb of the ongoing action - never drop it.
